record.title: microduck-eye-ring — the eye bezel: Pollen Robotics' published mesh `noenoeil` (Ø30.000 × 7.5 mm ring, Ø14.4 bore), mesh-backed part
record.why: GOAL.md finding 1 said the product's eye bezel is missing from the sim meshes; it is this mesh. Against the product photographs (out/head/head.json): front view eye OD / head width 0.3353 vs mesh 0.3226 (+1.16 mm implied on Ø30.000); profiles, scale-free, -0.02 ± 0.32 mm; verdict at the 1.5 mm rule CANNOT DETERMINE. bin/cad part:microduck-eye-ring (2026-09-02): PASS — Solid, valid, 1 shell, 984 faces, volume 4250.219 mm3, bbox 30.000 x 9.500 x 30.000 mm MEASURED off the finished solid. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 (lane A, tools/head_frontfit.py + head_width.py + head_width_verdict.py): the +1.16 mm above is SUPERSEDED — it came from a front-view read that used the photograph's accent TRIM BAND as the head width against the mesh's whole bottom-shell silhouette and compared a FILLED disc with an ANNULUS. Like for like on the head's outer silhouette, ring OD / head width is 0.3547 ± 0.0073 against 0.3318 on the mesh (+6.90 ± 2.74 %, the PAIR CANNOT DETERMINE); solving the pair with the head width taken from two RING-FREE lines (89.386 ± 1.815 mm) gives this ring 31.239 ± 1.065 mm against the mesh's 30.000 — +1.239 ± 1.065 mm, CANNOT DETERMINE at the 1.5 mm rule. The two profile photographs cannot measure the ring at all (their ring-scale sweeps end ON opposite ends of the swept range, 1.1200 and 0.9600). What settles it: a calliper across one product ring's OD.
record.origin_why: the geometry is the vendor's own published sim asset, loaded unchanged (tools/head_eye_ring_shelve.py, 2026-09-03). Not our design; usable to assemble, render, simulate and print; NOT licensed for sale (NC).
